terra.problem: Mark does not say Elijah and Moses came for the purpose of talking with Jesus, or that the disciples had nothing to say yet.
The descriptions of Elijah as a prophet and Moses as Israel's leader need references outside this passage.
Calling Abraham and David figures from Israel's story brings in facts outside the passage without references.
The references to Samuel and Isaiah as figures from Israel's story, Elijah as a prophet, and Moses as Israel's leader need references outside this passage.
Even as a guess, saying Peter was so busy planning for his guests that he forgot himself adds an action and a reason the text does not give.
Saying the sight would terrify anybody adds a universal claim and attributes the disciples' terror to a specific cause the text does not state.
The text does not say nobody was strutting or that they were too stunned to do so.
Saying this is Mark's way of keeping our eyes on Jesus assigns the writer an intention the passage does not state.
Saying the three barely had time to blink adds a length of time the text does not give.
Jesus gives a limit to His instruction, but the passage does not say their silence actually ended when He rose.
The passage says they kept the matter to themselves, but it does not say their silence lasted until the resurrection.
